all.doc: `first(list, condition)` returns the first element that satisfies the condition, `all(list, condition)` says whether they all satisfy it.

delete.doc: `put(l, index, value)` **replaces**; `put(l, index, value, 'insert')` slips it in before the index; `put(l, null, value)` appends; `put(l, null, other_list, 'extend')` appends the elements of the other list instead of the list itself. `delete(l, index)` removes — and unlike reading, which wraps indices, deleting an index that does not exist is an `IndexOutOfBoundsError`.

filter.doc: `map(list, expression)`, `filter(list, condition)`, `reduce(list, expression, initial)`. Inside the expression `_` is the current element, `_i` its index and `_a` the accumulator of `reduce`.

first.doc: `first(list, condition)` returns the first element that satisfies the condition, `all(list, condition)` says whether they all satisfy it.

has.doc: `has(l, index)` asks whether **that index** exists, not whether the list contains a value: for membership there is `(l ~ value) != null`, which returns the index or `null`.

join.doc: `join(separator, list)` joins the elements into a string.

length.doc: `range(end)`, `range(start, end)`, `range(start, end, step)` — lazy: the elements are produced as they go, so `range(1000000)` does not allocate a million values. A lazy list does not know its own length: `length(range(5))` does **not** answer `5`; to get it, materialise the list first with `slice(range(5), 0, 5)`.

synchronize.doc: `synchronize(lock, expression)` — the lock is reentrant (a synchronised function can call another one on the same lock) and fair (whoever waits gets in in the order they arrived, nobody is left out indefinitely).

task.doc: `task(function, ...arguments)` starts the execution on another thread and returns a handle. `task_join(t)` waits for the end and returns the value, `task_await(t)` waits without returning it, `task_completed(t)` says whether it has finished, `task_value(t)` reads the result when there is one. `task_count()` says how many tasks are in flight.

convert_date.doc: `time()` returns a monotonic counter in milliseconds with a decimal part — it is the one to use to measure how long something takes. `unix_time()` returns absolute time in milliseconds. `convert_date(timestamp)` breaks it into `[year, month, day, hour, minute, second, weekday, day_of_year]`, and the same function does the opposite starting from a list.

profile_expr.doc: `profile_expr(expression)` runs the expression repeatedly for a fixed interval and returns how many times it managed to: it is the quick way to compare two implementations without setting up a benchmark.

system_variable_get.doc: `system_variable_get(key)` and `system_variable_set(key, value)` read and write a space shared by every app on the same server.

system_variable_set.doc: `system_variable_get(key)` and `system_variable_set(key, value)` read and write a space shared by every app on the same server.

time.doc: `time()` returns a monotonic counter in milliseconds with a decimal part — it is the one to use to measure how long something takes. `unix_time()` returns absolute time in milliseconds. `convert_date(timestamp)` breaks it into `[year, month, day, hour, minute, second, weekday, day_of_year]`, and the same function does the opposite starting from a list.

type.doc: `type(value)` returns the name of the type. `var(name)` reads a variable by name and `vars(prefix)` lists the ones starting with a prefix — useful for debugging, not for normal logic, where a direct access is clearer and faster.

unix_time.doc: `time()` returns a monotonic counter in milliseconds with a decimal part — it is the one to use to measure how long something takes. `unix_time()` returns absolute time in milliseconds. `convert_date(timestamp)` breaks it into `[year, month, day, hour, minute, second, weekday, day_of_year]`, and the same function does the opposite starting from a list.

vars.doc: `type(value)` returns the name of the type. `var(name)` reads a variable by name and `vars(prefix)` lists the ones starting with a prefix — useful for debugging, not for normal logic, where a direct access is clearer and faster.

air.doc: ### `solid(pos)` · `air(pos)` · `liquid(pos)` Whether the block is solid, air, or a liquid.

blast_resistance.doc: ### `hardness(pos)` · `blast_resistance(pos)` How hard it is to break and how well it resists explosions.

block.doc: ### `block(pos)` The block at that position. Compared with a string it answers on the name.

block_data.doc: ### `block_data(pos)` The NBT of the block entity, `null` when that block does not have one.

block_light.doc: ### `light(pos)` · `block_light(pos)` · `sky_light(pos)` · `effective_light(pos)` · `emitted_light(pos)` The various light levels at that point: total, from blocks, from the sky, the one that counts for spawning, and the one the block itself emits.

block_list.doc: ### `block_list()` · `block_list(tag)` Every registered block, or the ones of a tag.

block_properties.doc: ### `block_properties(pos)` The names of the properties that block has.

block_sound.doc: ### `block_sound(pos)` · `material(pos)` · `map_colour(pos)` Sound group, material and colour on the map.

block_state.doc: ### `block_state(pos)` · `block_state(pos, property)` The properties of the block as a map, or the value of a single property.

block_tags.doc: ### `block_tags(pos)` · `block_tags(pos, tag)` The tags the block belongs to, or whether it belongs to the given one.

block_tick.doc: ### `update(pos)` · `block_tick(pos)` · `random_tick(pos)` Forces a block update, a scheduled tick or a random tick.

blocks_movement.doc: ### `blocks_movement(pos)` · `suffocates(pos)` Whether it stops movement, and whether it suffocates whoever is inside it.

brightness.doc: ### `see_sky(pos)` · `brightness(pos)` Whether the point sees the sky, and the brightness as a number between 0 and 1.

signatures: create_explosion(pos, power?, type?, fire?, source?, cause?)
create_explosion.doc: ### `create_explosion(pos, power?, type?, fire?, source?, cause?)` Blows something up at that point.

destroy.doc: ### `destroy(pos)` · `destroy(pos, -1)` · `destroy(pos, tool)` Breaks the block: with drops, without drops, or as if it had been broken with that tool.

effective_light.doc: ### `light(pos)` · `block_light(pos)` · `sky_light(pos)` · `effective_light(pos)` · `emitted_light(pos)` The various light levels at that point: total, from blocks, from the sky, the one that counts for spawning, and the one the block itself emits.

emitted_light.doc: ### `light(pos)` · `block_light(pos)` · `sky_light(pos)` · `effective_light(pos)` · `emitted_light(pos)` The various light levels at that point: total, from blocks, from the sky, the one that counts for spawning, and the one the block itself emits.

flammable.doc: ### `flammable(pos)` · `transparent(pos)` Whether it burns and whether it lets light through.

hardness.doc: ### `hardness(pos)` · `blast_resistance(pos)` How hard it is to break and how well it resists explosions.

harvest.doc: ### `harvest(player, pos)` Breaks the block the way that player would break it, respecting their tool and enchantments.

light.doc: ### `light(pos)` · `block_light(pos)` · `sky_light(pos)` · `effective_light(pos)` · `emitted_light(pos)` The various light levels at that point: total, from blocks, from the sky, the one that counts for spawning, and the one the block itself emits.

liquid.doc: ### `solid(pos)` · `air(pos)` · `liquid(pos)` Whether the block is solid, air, or a liquid.

map_colour.doc: ### `block_sound(pos)` · `material(pos)` · `map_colour(pos)` Sound group, material and colour on the map.

material.doc: ### `block_sound(pos)` · `material(pos)` · `map_colour(pos)` Sound group, material and colour on the map.

place_item.doc: ### `place_item(item, pos, face?, consider_flags?)` Uses an item on a block, the way a player clicking on it would.

pos.doc: ### `pos(entity)` · `pos_offset(pos, direction, how_much?)` The position of an entity, and a position shifted in a direction.

pos_offset.doc: ### `pos(entity)` · `pos_offset(pos, direction, how_much?)` The position of an entity, and a position shifted in a direction.

power.doc: ### `ticks_randomly(pos)` · `power(pos)` Whether it gets random ticks, and the redstone signal it emits.

property.doc: ### `property(pos, name)` The value of a property, `null` when the block does not have it.

random_tick.doc: ### `update(pos)` · `block_tick(pos)` · `random_tick(pos)` Forces a block update, a scheduled tick or a random tick.

see_sky.doc: ### `see_sky(pos)` · `brightness(pos)` Whether the point sees the sky, and the brightness as a number between 0 and 1.

set.doc: ### `set(pos, block, properties...)` Places a block. The properties are passed as name/value pairs, or as a map. A property the block does not have is an error, with a suggestion of the right name.

sky_light.doc: ### `light(pos)` · `block_light(pos)` · `sky_light(pos)` · `effective_light(pos)` · `emitted_light(pos)` The various light levels at that point: total, from blocks, from the sky, the one that counts for spawning, and the one the block itself emits.

solid.doc: ### `solid(pos)` · `air(pos)` · `liquid(pos)` Whether the block is solid, air, or a liquid.

suffocates.doc: ### `blocks_movement(pos)` · `suffocates(pos)` Whether it stops movement, and whether it suffocates whoever is inside it.

ticks_randomly.doc: ### `ticks_randomly(pos)` · `power(pos)` Whether it gets random ticks, and the redstone signal it emits.

transparent.doc: ### `flammable(pos)` · `transparent(pos)` Whether it burns and whether it lets light through.

update.doc: ### `update(pos)` · `block_tick(pos)` · `random_tick(pos)` Forces a block update, a scheduled tick or a random tick.

without_updates.doc: ### `without_updates(expression)` Runs the expression without propagating block updates: useful to build in bulk without setting off redstone and falling blocks at every step.

add_chunk_ticket.doc: ### `chunk_tickets()` · `add_chunk_ticket(pos, type, radius)` The tickets keeping chunks loaded, and how to add one.

biome.doc: ### `biome(pos)` · `biome(name, property)` · `set_biome(pos, name, update?)` Reads the biome of a point, queries the properties of a biome, or changes it.

chunk_tickets.doc: ### `chunk_tickets()` · `add_chunk_ticket(pos, type, radius)` The tickets keeping chunks loaded, and how to add one.

current_dimension.doc: ### `current_dimension()` The dimension the script is running in.

day_time.doc: ### `world_time()` · `day_time()` · `day_time(new_value)` The total time of the world and the time of day; with an argument it sets the time.

enable_hidden_dimensions.doc: ### `view_distance()` · `enable_hidden_dimensions()` The render distance of the server, and turning on the normally hidden dimensions.

game_tick.doc: ### `game_tick()` · `game_tick(max_milliseconds)` Forces the server to advance by one tick. With the argument, it keeps running ticks until it has used up that time. It is what makes the game move forward from a script running inside a tick.

generation_status.doc: ### `is_chunk_generated(pos)` · `generation_status(pos)` Whether the chunk exists on disk, and how far its generation got.

in_dimension.doc: ### `in_dimension(dimension, expression)` Evaluates the expression as if it were in another dimension: every world function inside it looks there.

in_slime_chunk.doc: ### `inhabited_time(pos)` · `in_slime_chunk(pos)` · `spawn_potential(pos)` How much it has been lived in, whether it is a slime chunk, and the spawn potential computed by the game.

inhabited_time.doc: ### `inhabited_time(pos)` · `in_slime_chunk(pos)` · `spawn_potential(pos)` How much it has been lived in, whether it is a slime chunk, and the spawn potential computed by the game.

is_chunk_generated.doc: ### `is_chunk_generated(pos)` · `generation_status(pos)` Whether the chunk exists on disk, and how far its generation got.

last_tick_times.doc: ### `tick_time()` · `last_tick_times()` The current tick of the server, and the times of the last 100 ticks in milliseconds.

loaded.doc: ### `loaded(pos)` · `loaded_status(pos)` · `loaded_ep(pos)` Whether the chunk is loaded, in which state it is, and whether it is loaded for entity processing.

loaded_ep.doc: ### `loaded(pos)` · `loaded_status(pos)` · `loaded_ep(pos)` Whether the chunk is loaded, in which state it is, and whether it is loaded for entity processing.

loaded_status.doc: ### `loaded(pos)` · `loaded_status(pos)` · `loaded_ep(pos)` Whether the chunk is loaded, in which state it is, and whether it is loaded for entity processing.

plop.doc: ### `plop(pos, what)` Places a feature or a structure of the generator at that point (trees, geysers, villages...).

poi.doc: ### `poi(pos)` · `poi(pos, radius, sort?, type?, state?)` The points of interest (beds, work stations, portals) in an area.

relight.doc: ### `relight(pos)` Recomputes the light around a point.

reload_chunk.doc: ### `reload_chunk(pos)` · `reset_chunk(pos)` Sends the chunk back to the clients, or regenerates it from scratch.

reset_chunk.doc: ### `reload_chunk(pos)` · `reset_chunk(pos)` Sends the chunk back to the clients, or regenerates it from scratch.

sample_noise.doc: ### `sample_noise(pos, type)` · `sample_noise()` Samples a density function of the generator at that point; without arguments it lists the available names.

seed.doc: ### `seed()` · `save()` The seed of the world, and a forced save to disk.

set_structure.doc: ### `set_structure(pos, name)` · `set_structure(pos, name, null)` Generates a structure, or removes its reference.

spawn_potential.doc: ### `inhabited_time(pos)` · `in_slime_chunk(pos)` · `spawn_potential(pos)` How much it has been lived in, whether it is a slime chunk, and the spawn potential computed by the game.

structure_eligibility.doc: ### `structure_eligibility(pos, type?, details?)` Whether a structure *could* generate in that chunk, without generating it.

structure_references.doc: ### `structure_references(pos)` · `structure_references(pos, name)` The chunks referring to the structures of that point.

structures.doc: ### `structures(pos)` · `structures(pos, name)` The structures covering that point.

view_distance.doc: ### `view_distance()` · `enable_hidden_dimensions()` The render distance of the server, and turning on the normally hidden dimensions.

diamond.doc: ### `rect(centre, radius?, skip?)` · `diamond(centre, radius?, height?)` The positions of a box or of an octahedron, as a lazy list: they are consumed as they go, without building the whole volume in memory.

rect.doc: ### `rect(centre, radius?, skip?)` · `diamond(centre, radius?, height?)` The positions of a box or of an octahedron, as a lazy list: they are consumed as they go, without building the whole volume in memory.

scan.doc: ### `scan(centre, radii, expression)` · `scan(centre, radii_down, radii_up, expression)` Walks over a box around the centre. The radii are **three numbers** or a triple, like positions: `scan(pos, [2, 1, 2], ...)` and `scan(pos, 2, 1, 2, ...)` are the same thing. With two groups of radii the volume can be asymmetric.

volume.doc: ### `volume(from, to, expression)` Like `scan`, but the volume is given with two corners instead of centre and radius.

core.mc.entity.doc: finding, creating and modifying entities and players

create_marker.doc: ### `create_marker(name, pos, block?, tag?)` · `remove_all_markers()` Markers shown while debugging a script; `remove_all_markers` cleans up the ones of the app.

entity_area.doc: ### `entity_area(type, centre, radius)` The entities of a type inside an area.

entity_event.doc: ### `entity_event(entity, event, function, fixed_arguments...)` Attaches a handler to *that* entity: `on_tick`, `on_removed`, `on_death`, `on_damage`, `on_move`. The handler lives inside the entity, so it follows it between worlds and disappears with it. Passing `null` in place of the function removes it.

entity_id.doc: ### `entity_id(id | uuid)` · `entity_types(type?)` An entity from its numeric id or uuid, and the registered entity types.

entity_list.doc: ### `entity_list(type)` Every entity of a type in the world (`'*'` for all of them, `'!player'` for everything but players).

entity_load_handler.doc: ### `entity_load_handler(types, function)` Calls `function(entity)` every time an entity of one of those types appears. `types` is a type or a list of types (`'zombie'`, `['zombie', 'minecraft:husk']`); with `null` you hear about all of them.

entity_selector.doc: ### `entity_selector(selector)` The entities a vanilla selector (`@e[type=cow,distance=..10]`) would pick.

entity_types.doc: ### `entity_id(id | uuid)` · `entity_types(type?)` An entity from its numeric id or uuid, and the registered entity types.

has_client.doc: ### `has_client(player)` Whether that player has Blossom on the client too — that is, whether they will see the shapes of [`core.mc.shape`](core.mc.shape.md) really drawn instead of approximated with particles.

modify.doc: ### `modify(entity, what, value...)` Writes an attribute: `pos`, `motion`, `motion_x`/`y`/`z`, `custom_name`, `health`, `food`, `air`, `gamemode`, `nbt`, `effect`, `nbt_merge`, `persistence`, `jump`, `kill`, `dismount`, `mount`, `tag`, `fire`, `silent`, `gravity`, `invulnerable`, `pickup_delay`, `portal_cooldown`, and others.

player.doc: ### `player()` · `player(name)` · `player('all' | 'survival' | 'creative' | 'spectating' | ...)` The player running the script, one by name, or the list of the ones in a category.

query.doc: ### `query(entity, what, arguments...)` Reads an attribute. There are many: `pos`, `x`/`y`/`z`, `motion`, `name`, `uuid`, `health`, `food`, `air`, `on_ground`, `sneaking`, `sprinting`, `gamemode`, `holds`, `inventory`, `effect`, `nbt`, `dimension`, `target`, `brain`, `look`, `facing`, `age`, `fire`, `is_burning`, `hunger`, `saturation`, `portal_cooldown`, and others. `query(entity, 'nbt')` gives a

remove_all_markers.doc: ### `create_marker(name, pos, block?, tag?)` · `remove_all_markers()` Markers shown while debugging a script; `remove_all_markers` cleans up the ones of the app.

spawn.doc: ### `spawn(type, pos, nbt?)` Creates an entity. The NBT is the one the game would use in a `/summon` command.

component_list.doc: ### `component_list()` The ids of every component this game knows.

crafting_remaining_item.doc: ### `stack_limit(item)` · `crafting_remaining_item(item)` How high it stacks, and what is left after using it in a recipe (the empty bucket, say).

drop_item.doc: ### `drop_item(inventory, slot, count?)` Throws the content of a slot on the ground.

inventory_find.doc: ### `inventory_find(inventory, item, from_slot?)` The first slot containing that item, `null` when there is none.

inventory_get.doc: ### `inventory_get(inventory, slot?)` The content of a slot, or the whole inventory when the slot is not given.

inventory_has_items.doc: ### `inventory_has_items(inventory, items...)` Whether the inventory holds everything needed.

inventory_remove.doc: ### `inventory_remove(inventory, item, count?)` Takes items out of the inventory, wherever they are.

inventory_set.doc: ### `inventory_set(inventory, slot, count, item?, nbt?)` Writes a slot. A count of `0` empties it.

inventory_size.doc: ### `inventory_size(inventory)` How many slots it has, `null` when there is no inventory there.

item_category.doc: ### `item_list(tag?)` · `item_tags(item, tag?)` · `item_category(item)` The registered items, the tags of an item, and its category in the creative menu.

item_component.doc: ### `item_component(item, name, default?)` A single component, or `null` when that stack does not have it.

item_components.doc: ### `item_components(item, default?)` Every component, as a map from id to value. With `default` true it reads the ones the **item has of its own** instead of the ones this stack carries: it is the comparison between the two that says whether a value was set on purpose or is the one every item of that kind has.

item_display_name.doc: ### `item_display_name(item)` The name shown in game, translated.

item_list.doc: ### `item_list(tag?)` · `item_tags(item, tag?)` · `item_category(item)` The registered items, the tags of an item, and its category in the creative menu.

item_tags.doc: ### `item_list(tag?)` · `item_tags(item, tag?)` · `item_category(item)` The registered items, the tags of an item, and its category in the creative menu.

recipe_data.doc: ### `recipe_data(item, type?)` The recipes producing that item: ingredients, result and type.

set_item_component.doc: ### `set_item_component(item, name, value)` The item with that component changed; with `value` at `null` it removes it. It returns a copy and does not touch the original — an item read from an inventory is already a copy, and pretending that writing into it changes the world would be worse than not being able to.

stack_limit.doc: ### `stack_limit(item)` · `crafting_remaining_item(item)` How high it stacks, and what is left after using it in a recipe (the empty bucket, say).

core.mc.structure.doc: saving, placing and comparing structure templates

signatures: structure_load(name, pos, rotation?, mirror?, with_entities?, integrity?, seed?)
structure_load.doc: ### `structure_load(name, pos, rotation?, mirror?, with_entities?, integrity?, seed?)` Places the template. It returns whether it succeeded, `null` when the template does not exist.

structure_matches.doc: **`pos` is always the minimum corner of the result**, rotated or mirrored as it may be. Rotation and mirroring would turn the structure *around* the anchor, and without this correction the same call with a different rotation would end up somewhere else — which nobody finds obvious. It is also what makes `structure_load` and `structure_matches` reciprocal.

structure_save.doc: ### `structure_save(name, from, to, with_entities?)` Saves the volume between the two corners (inclusive) as a template. `with_entities` is `false` by default. It returns whether the save succeeded.

structure_size.doc: ### `structure_size(name, rotation?)` The size of the template as `[x, y, z]`, taking the rotation into account, or `null` when it does not exist.

core.mc.shape.doc: showing what a script is computing

clear_shapes.doc: ### `clear_shapes()` Forgets the shapes still waiting to be redrawn as particles. It does not remove the ones already sent to a client, which expire on their own.

draw_shape.doc: Whoever writes the script does not have to know who has what: `draw_shape` decides on its own, player by player, and returns how many of them got it as a real shape. If you need to know beforehand there is `has_client(player)`, in [`core.mc.entity`](core.mc.entity.md) — it is a question about a player, not about the drawing.

close_screen.doc: ### `close_screen(screen)` Closes it. The player goes back to their own inventory.

create_screen.doc: ### `create_screen(player, type, title, callback?)` Opens a screen. The types are the vanilla ones: `generic_9x1`..`generic_9x6`, `generic_3x3`, `anvil`, `beacon`, `blast_furnace`, `brewing_stand`, `crafting`, `enchantment`, `furnace`, `grindstone`, `hopper`, `lectern`, `loom`, `merchant`, `shulker_box`, `smithing`, `smoker`, `cartography`, `stonecutter`.

screen_property.doc: ### `screen_property(screen, property)` · `screen_property(screen, property, value)` Reads or writes a property of the screen (the level of an enchantment, the progress of a furnace, the fuel...).

bossbar.doc: ### `bossbar()` · `bossbar(name)` · `bossbar(name, property, value?)` The existing bars, the creation of a bar, and its properties: `name`, `color`, `style`, `value`, `max`, `visible`, `players`, `add_player`, `remove`.

scoreboard.doc: ### `scoreboard()` · `scoreboard(objective)` · `scoreboard(objective, who)` · `scoreboard(objective, who, value)` The existing objectives, the scores of an objective, the score of one, or the assignment of a score.

scoreboard_add.doc: ### `scoreboard_add(objective, criterion?)` · `scoreboard_remove(objective)` · `scoreboard_remove(objective, who)` Creates an objective, deletes it, or removes the score of a single one.

scoreboard_display.doc: ### `scoreboard_display(slot, objective?)` Shows an objective in a slot (`'sidebar'`, `'list'`, `'belowName'`, or a team colour).

scoreboard_property.doc: ### `scoreboard_property(objective, property, value?)` Reads or writes the properties of an objective: `display_name`, `criterion`, `render_type`.

scoreboard_remove.doc: ### `scoreboard_add(objective, criterion?)` · `scoreboard_remove(objective)` · `scoreboard_remove(objective, who)` Creates an objective, deletes it, or removes the score of a single one.

team_add.doc: ### `team_add(team)` · `team_add(team, who)` · `team_remove(team)` · `team_leave(who)` Creates a team, adds somebody to it, disbands it, or makes somebody leave the one they are in.

team_leave.doc: ### `team_add(team)` · `team_add(team, who)` · `team_remove(team)` · `team_leave(who)` Creates a team, adds somebody to it, disbands it, or makes somebody leave the one they are in.

team_list.doc: ### `team_list()` · `team_list(team)` The teams, or the members of a team.

team_property.doc: ### `team_property(team, property, value?)` Reads or writes the properties of a team: `collisionRule`, `color`, `displayName`, `friendlyFire`, `nametagVisibility`, `deathMessageVisibility`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `seeFriendlyInvisibles`.

team_remove.doc: ### `team_add(team)` · `team_add(team, who)` · `team_remove(team)` · `team_leave(who)` Creates a team, adds somebody to it, disbands it, or makes somebody leave the one they are in.

core.mc.nbt.doc: the raw data of the game

encode_nbt.doc: ### `encode_nbt(value, force?)` From Blossom values to NBT. With `force` true, what has no NBT shape becomes its string instead of failing the conversion.

escape_nbt.doc: ### `escape_nbt(string)` Puts a string in the form the game would write it inside a tag.

nbt.doc: ### `nbt(value)` Builds an NBT value from a string in command format, from a map or from a list.

nbt_storage.doc: ### `nbt_storage()` · `nbt_storage(key)` · `nbt_storage(key, value)` The NBT storage of the world, the one the commands call `data storage`: it is the way to exchange data with functions and datapacks.

parse_nbt.doc: ### `parse_nbt(nbt)` The opposite: from NBT to ordinary Blossom values (maps, lists, numbers, strings).

tag_matches.doc: ### `tag_matches(tag, predicate, respect_lists?)` Whether a tag satisfies a partial predicate, with the same semantics as the vanilla commands.

signatures: display_title(targets, type, text?, fade_in?, stay?, fade_out?)
display_title.doc: ### `display_title(targets, type, text?, fade_in?, stay?, fade_out?)` Writes big on the screen. The types are `'title'`, `'subtitle'`, `'actionbar'`, `'player_list_header'`, `'player_list_footer'`, and `'clear'`/`'reset'` to remove.

format.doc: ### `format(pieces...)` Formatted text. Every piece is `'style text'`, where the style is made of letters:

hud.doc: ### `hud(players, text, duration?)` · `hud(player)` A line of text above the hotbar.

print.doc: ### `print(message)` · `print(target, message)` Writes a message: to whoever launched the script, or to a given target. The target is a player or a **list of players**, so the list `entity.player('all')` returns goes in as it is, with no loop around it. It returns the message, so it can be slipped in the middle of an expression without breaking it.

signatures: particle(name, pos, how_many?, spread?, speed?, player?)
particle.doc: ### `particle()` · `particle(name, pos, how_many?, spread?, speed?, player?)` Without arguments, the available particles. With the arguments, it spawns some at a point - for a single player, when one is named.

particle_box.doc: ### `particle_box(name, corner_a, corner_b, density?, player?)` The twelve edges of a box: it is the quick way to show the area a script is working on.

particle_line.doc: ### `particle_line(name, from, to, density?, player?)` A line of particles between two points. It returns how many it sent.

post_effect.doc: ### `post_effect(players, action, effect?)` The post-processing shaders of one or more players, that is, what the game calls `/posteffect`.

sound.doc: ### `sound()` · `sound(name, pos, volume?, pitch?, category?)` Without arguments, the available sounds. With the arguments, it plays a sound at a point for whoever is close enough to hear it.

available.doc: ### `available()` · `listeners(event)` · `describe(event)` The names of the events, how many listen to an event, and its card: arity, cancellability, listeners.

describe.doc: ### `available()` · `listeners(event)` · `describe(event)` The names of the events, how many listen to an event, and its card: arity, cancellability, listeners.

handle_event.doc: ### `handle_event(event, function, fixed_arguments...)` Like `on`, but it also takes a name the game does not know: that becomes an **application event**, declared by the first app that listens to it.

listeners.doc: ### `available()` · `listeners(event)` · `describe(event)` The names of the events, how many listen to an event, and its card: arity, cancellability, listeners.

off.doc: ### `off()` · `off(event)` Removes every handler of the app, or only the ones of an event.

on.doc: ### `on(event, function)` · `on(event, function, fixed_arguments)` · `on(event, function, fixed_arguments, player)` Registers a handler. The fixed arguments arrive after the ones of the event. With the fourth argument the handler fires only for that player.

schedule.doc: ### `schedule(delay_in_ticks, function, arguments...)` Calls a function N ticks from now. The times are in ticks and not in milliseconds: a script waiting twenty ticks waits the same amount of *game* time even when the server slows down.

signal_event.doc: ### `signal_event(event, player_or_null, arguments...)` Raises an application event. It returns how many apps were listening, `null` when that event does not exist. It is the way to make two apps talk without either knowing the functions of the other.

core.mc.file.doc: the data of the app on disk

create_datapack.doc: ### `create_datapack(name, content)` Creates a datapack from the given content (a map of paths -> files) and enables it.

delete_file.doc: ### `delete_file(name, type)` · `list_files(folder, type)` Deletes a file, and lists the ones in a folder.

list_files.doc: ### `delete_file(name, type)` · `list_files(folder, type)` Deletes a file, and lists the ones in a folder.

load_app_data.doc: ### `load_app_data()` · `load_app_data(name)` · `store_app_data(data)` · `store_app_data(data, name)` The state of the app in NBT, saved and read back without thinking about paths. Without a name it is the default state file of the app.

read_file.doc: ### `read_file(name, type)` Reads a file. The types are `'text'` (a list of lines), `'json'`, `'nbt'`, `'raw'`, `'shared_text'`, `'shared_json'`, `'shared_nbt'`, `'shared_raw'`.

store_app_data.doc: ### `load_app_data()` · `load_app_data(name)` · `store_app_data(data)` · `store_app_data(data, name)` The state of the app in NBT, saved and read back without thinking about paths. Without a name it is the default state file of the app.

write_file.doc: ### `write_file(name, type, data)` Writes, or appends when the type is textual.

get_mob_counts.doc: ### `get_mob_counts()` · `get_mob_counts(category)` How many mobs of each category there are, and how many the cap would allow.

logger.doc: ### `logger(message)` · `logger(level, message)` Writes to the log of the server. The levels are `'error'`, `'warn'`, `'info'`, `'debug'`.

run.doc: ### `run(command)` Runs a vanilla command with the permissions of the app and collects its outcome, instead of printing it in chat. It returns `[code, output]`.

statistic.doc: ### `statistic(player, category, entry)` A statistic of a player (`'used'`, `'mined'`, `'killed'`, `'custom'`, ...).

system_info.doc: ### `system_info()` · `system_info(key)` Information about the server and the process: memory, threads, version, loaded mods, uptime, loaded worlds, loaded apps. Without arguments it lists the available keys.

task_join.doc: ### `task_join(task)` Waits for a task started with `core.task`, but from the server thread: it is the variant that knows how to wait without blocking the tick.
